ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Scapula fractures: 3

Radiographs show a scapular fracture extending toward the glenoid. The surgeon needs precise information about articular displacement and fracture configuration. Which listed imaging method best supports assessment of this complex bony anatomy?

  1. Protected early motion when stability permits
  2. Assess associated injuries beyond the visible fracture
  3. CT to define the injury and adjacent structures
  4. Document neurovascular status before and after intervention
  5. Urgent specialist evaluation and controlled treatment
Answer and explanation

CT to define the injury and adjacent structures

CT helps evaluate complex bony anatomy, articular involvement or sternoclavicular relationships when indicated.

Option explanations

CT to define the injury and adjacent structures: CT helps evaluate complex bony anatomy, articular involvement or sternoclavicular relationships when indicated.

Document neurovascular status before and after intervention: Serial motor, sensory and perfusion examinations establish baseline function and detect new deficits after reduction or splinting. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Urgent specialist evaluation and controlled treatment: Threatened neurovascular or mediastinal structures require urgent appropriately supported care, not casual manipulation. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Protected early motion when stability permits: Appropriate early motion reduces stiffness; timing depends on stability and the treatment plan. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.

Assess associated injuries beyond the visible fracture: High-energy injuries can coexist with chest, neurovascular or adjacent-joint injuries that alter priorities. This does not best answer the specific question in this case.
